    89→### Zustand Store Pattern

    91→For annotation state management:
    92→

    94→interface AnnotationStore {

    96→  selectedAnnotation: string | null;

    98→

   117→class PlaybookDatabase extends Dexie {

   122→    this.version(2).stores({

   124→    });
   125→  }
   126→}

   132→- Version migrations for schema changes

   146→      ))}
   147→    </group>
   148→  );
   149→}
   150→```

   153→- Use React Three Fiber declarative components
   154→- Leverage @react-three/drei helpers for text, shapes
   155→- Use groups for logical organization
   156→- Keep rendering logic separate from interaction logic

    87→## Patterns to Follow
    88→
    89→### Zustand Store Pattern
    90→
    91→For annotation state management:
    92→
    93→```typescript
    94→interface AnnotationStore {
    95→  annotations: Annotation[];
    96→  selectedAnnotation: string | null;
    97→  activeToolType: AnnotationType | null;
    98→
    99→  addAnnotation: (annotation: Annotation) => void;

   103→  setActiveTool: (type: AnnotationType | null) => void;
   104→}
   105→```

   108→- Use immer for immutable state updates (Zustand middleware)
   109→- Keep store focused on annotation-specific state
   110→- Separate concerns: UI state vs data state
   111→
   112→### Dexie Schema Pattern
   113→
   114→For annotation persistence:
   115→
   116→```typescript
   117→class PlaybookDatabase extends Dexie {
   118→  annotations!: Table<Annotation>;
   119→
   120→  constructor() {
   121→    super('PlaybookDB');
   122→    this.version(2).stores({
   123→      annotations: '++id, playbookId, type, createdAt'
   124→    });
   125→  }
   126→}
   127→```
   128→
   129→**Key Points:**
   130→- Use auto-incrementing primary keys
   131→- Index fields used for queries (playbookId for filtering)
   132→- Version migrations for schema changes
   133→
   134→### Three.js Component Pattern
   135→
   136→For rendering annotations in the 3D scene:
   137→
   138→```typescript
   139→function AnnotationLayer() {
   140→  const annotations = useAnnotationStore(state => state.annotations);
   141→
   142→  return (
   143→    <group name="annotation-layer">
   144→      {annotations.map(annotation => (
   145→        <AnnotationRenderer key={annotation.id} annotation={annotation} />
   146→      ))}
   147→    </group>
   148→  );
   149→}
   150→```
   151→
   152→**Key Points:**
   153→- Use React Three Fiber declarative components
   154→- Leverage @react-three/drei helpers for text, shapes
   155→- Use groups for logical organization
   156→- Keep rendering logic separate from interaction logic
   157→

   159→
   160→### Functional Requirements
   161→
   162→1. **Text Label Annotations**
   163→   - Description: Allow placement of text labels at any 3D position on the field
   164→   - Acceptance: User can click "Text" tool, click field location, enter text, and see label rendered with editable text and position
   165→
   166→2. **Arrow Annotations**
   167→   - Description: Draw directional arrows between two points on the field
   168→   - Acceptance: User can click "Arrow" tool, click start point, drag to end point, and see arrow with adjustable endpoints
   169→
   170→3. **Zone Highlighting**
   171→   - Description: Create semi-transparent shapes to highlight areas of the field
   172→   - Acceptance: User can click "Zone" tool, define shape bounds (rectangle/circle), and see semi-transparent overlay with adjustable size/position
   173→
   174→4. **Free-hand Drawing**
   175→   - Description: Allow direct sketching on the field surface
   176→   - Acceptance: User can click "Draw" tool, drag mouse to create continuous path, and see rendered stroke with smooth curves
   177→

   181→

   184→   - Acceptance: Click annotation to select, use delete key or button to remove, drag handles to modify position/size/endpoints
